newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields track Germany higher.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields track Germany higher.

text.p: Swedish bond yields tracked the German market to trade higher at midday on Tuesday after starting lower.
"We have followed Germany closely today and the spread (to long German yields) has been constant at 108 basis points," one dealer said.
The six-month T-bill rate rose one basis point to 4.15 percent and the ten-year bond yield advanced one to 6.78.
The crown firmed against the mark from a softer opening to trade around late Monday levels. The currency was quoted at 4.4745 to the mark compared to 4.4780 late on Monday.
The crown benefited from a general mark softening after European Union members agreed on a stability pact on Monday.
"The mark is generally somewhat weaker but it is an internal European movement. People are for example buying Italian lira for marks," a dealer said.
Market players are eyeing U.S. data this afternoon with May consumer prices and new housing starts due at 1230 GMT and industrial producion and capacity utilisation due at 1315 GMT.
